title: Teacher-based bias, the imposter phenomenon, and internalizing distress among adolescents in Germany
abstract: Abstract Teacher-based bias is an increasingly recognized psychosocial stressor in educational settings, yet its associations with the imposter phenomenon and internalizing distress remain poorly understood, particularly with regard to racialized identity and gender identity as influencing factors. The present cross-sectional study examined these associations in a diverse sample of N = 575 adolescents (Mean age = 16.05; 52% girls*; 41% BIPoC) recruited from seven secondary schools in Berlin, Germany. Exploratory group comparisons revealed meaningful differences across gender identity and racialized groups. We tested a moderated mediation model in which imposter phenomenon mediated the teacher-based bias–distress association, with (ethnic-)racialized identity and gender identity as moderators. Teacher-based bias was positively associated with internalizing distress, but not with imposter phenomenon, and the moderated mediation model was not supported. Imposter phenomenon, however, emerged as a strong independent correlate of internalizing distress. Findings underscore the psychological relevance of teacher-based bias and imposter-related cognitions for adolescent mental health and point to the need for equitable school environments and targeted psychological support.
